title: Support for continued coverage of SI joint injections
comment: As a practicing pain management physician, I strongly support continued Medicare coverage of sacroiliac joint injections under this LCD. These injections are essential and beneficial for patients whose chronic low back pain has not responded to conservative care. Restricting access would harm treatment outcomes for elderly beneficiaries.

title: Opposed to the proposed frequency limits
comment: The proposed limit on the number of SIJ injections per year is unworkable and harmful. Many patients require repeat sacroiliac joint injections to maintain function, and this arbitrary restriction will reduce access to necessary treatment and worsen patient outcomes.

title: Documentation requirements are excessive
comment: The new prior authorization and documentation requirements for sacroiliac joint injections impose an excessive administrative burden on physician practices. The additional paperwork and reporting are onerous, time-consuming, and duplicative of records we already maintain.

title: Question on diagnostic block criteria
comment: I would like clarification on whether a dual diagnostic block is required before a therapeutic SIJ injection is covered. The draft LCD language is unclear and ambiguous on this point and the documentation expectations should be defined more precisely.

title: Reimbursement cuts are unsustainable
comment: The proposed reimbursement reduction for sacroiliac joint injection procedures is costly and unsustainable for small practices. The payment cut does not cover the cost of imaging guidance, supplies, and staff, and will force providers to stop offering this service.

title: This LCD exceeds statutory authority
comment: The contractor's proposed non-coverage of certain SIJ injection techniques is an unlawful overreach that exceeds the statutory authority granted under the Medicare program. This rulemaking is arbitrary and capricious and conflicts with the governing statute.

title: Rural patients will lose access
comment: In our rural region, sacroiliac joint injections are one of the few interventional options available. The proposed coverage restrictions will create barriers to access for underserved beneficiaries who cannot travel long distances for alternative care.

title: Evidence supports the policy
comment: I support this thoughtful and balanced LCD. The evidence-based criteria for sacroiliac joint injections are reasonable and will improve the appropriateness of care while protecting patient safety. The coverage framework is clear and workable.

title: Neutral comment requesting effective date detail
comment: Please confirm the effective date for the updated sacroiliac joint injection coverage criteria and whether claims already submitted will be processed under the prior policy. This is a procedural question about implementation timing.

title: Strong support from patient advocate
comment: As a beneficiary who has benefited greatly from SIJ injections, I am grateful for continued coverage. This treatment restored my mobility and quality of life. I appreciate CMS preserving access to this essential and effective therapy for seniors.

title: Prior authorization will delay care
comment: Requiring prior authorization for every sacroiliac joint injection is a bureaucratic barrier that will delay necessary treatment. The administrative process is burdensome and the added paperwork jeopardizes timely access to pain relief for patients.

title: Cost savings concern
comment: While I understand the budget pressures, restricting SIJ injection coverage to reduce spending is short-sighted. The cost of untreated chronic pain, including increased opioid use and disability, will exceed any savings from limiting these procedures.

title: Support with minor edits
comment: Overall this is a sound and beneficial policy for sacroiliac joint injections. I support the clinical criteria but recommend clarifying the imaging guidance language so that providers and beneficiaries have clear expectations about coverage.

title: Opposed: harms access for dual-eligible patients
comment: This restrictive LCD will reduce coverage and create access barriers for low-income dual-eligible beneficiaries who rely on sacroiliac joint injections. The policy is harmful and will worsen health disparities in vulnerable populations.

title: Administrative process redundant
comment: The required documentation for SIJ injections duplicates information already captured in the medical record. This redundant reporting requirement adds administrative overhead and staff time without improving the quality or safety of care.

title: Legal authority question
comment: On what statutory basis does the contractor assert authority to categorically deny coverage for image-guided sacroiliac joint injections? This determination appears to exceed the agency's rulemaking authority and is legally questionable.

title: Beneficial for veterans and seniors
comment: Sacroiliac joint injections have been beneficial and effective for many of my older patients, including veterans with degenerative joint disease. I strongly support maintaining access to this valuable treatment and commend CMS for the clear criteria.

title: Neutral data request
comment: Could the contractor publish the utilization data and evidence review used to develop the sacroiliac joint injection coverage criteria? I am requesting the underlying analysis for transparency before forming a position on the proposal.

title: Excessive cost burden on practices
comment: The combination of lower reimbursement and higher documentation cost makes sacroiliac joint injections financially unworkable for independent practices. This funding shortfall is burdensome and will reduce the availability of the procedure.

title: Support evidence-based limits
comment: I support reasonable, evidence-based limits on sacroiliac joint injections to ensure appropriate use. A requirement to document a positive diagnostic response is sensible and protects patients from unnecessary procedures while preserving access for those who benefit.

title: Opposed to non-coverage of lateral branch blocks
comment: Excluding lateral branch blocks related to sacroiliac joint pain from coverage is harmful and not supported by the clinical evidence. This restriction will deny effective treatment and is an unnecessary barrier to appropriate patient care.

title: Implementation timeline too short
comment: The implementation timeline for the revised SIJ injection LCD does not give practices adequate time to update workflow, billing, and documentation systems. The compliance burden of this short timeframe is excessive and impractical.

title: Grateful for coverage clarity
comment: Thank you for clarifying the coverage criteria for sacroiliac joint injections. The clear and transparent guidance is helpful and will improve consistency. This is a positive and meaningful step that benefits both providers and beneficiaries.

title: Concern about access in underserved areas
comment: Limiting the providers who may perform covered sacroiliac joint injections will restrict access and coverage in underserved communities. Patients already face barriers, and this proposal will worsen availability of care where it is most needed.
